page: Amazon Web Services c8id.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores with a dedicated allocation running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The memory configuration consists of 384.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled directly with the instance, featuring 11400 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, while network connectivity delivers a baseline bandwidth of 75 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. This compute density is complemented by high-speed memory bandwidth, reaching uncached read speeds of 586.52 GB/sec and write speeds of 251.15 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core results falling in the middle 50% tier. The processor includes Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which accelerate workloads like LLM inference, where prompt processing speeds for medium and large models rank in the top 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c8id.48xlarge offers high compute and local storage density on the Nitro hypervisor, reducing the need for external storage attachments for data-intensive tasks. The combination of high-speed DDR5 memory, massive local NVMe storage, and top-tier database operation benchmarks makes this instance type suitable for large-scale database deployments, Redis key-value stores, multi-threaded decompression, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
